title: Lazy inputs and check_lazy_status
hook: A switch with two expensive branches should only pay for one. Lazy inputs make that happen, at the cost of visiting your node twice.

verified.claim: A required lazy input with no Python default worked: on the first visit it arrived as None.
verified.ref: a V3 test node through PromptExecutor on a CPU

verified.claim: With a lazy switch, the real order was check, branch A, check, run, and branch B never ran.
verified.ref: V1 and V3 test nodes through PromptExecutor on a CPU

verified.claim: Asking for an input with no wire fails with: Node 5 says it needs input a, but there is no input to that node at all.
A required input marked lazy and left unwired still gives required_input_missing.
Core's If/Else Switch runs only the side it uses: with switch True, ImageInvert ran once, and with switch False it did not run.
verified.ref: graph f_lazy_switch with a counter on ImageInvert

verified.claim: The docs say lazy has very little cost and that check_lazy_status may be called many times.

unchecked: We didn't measure the cost of the second visit. It is one extra Python call, and we didn't time it.
How lazy interacts with INPUT_IS_LIST comes from the docstring in _io.py (unevaluated inputs arrive as (None,)). We did not run that combination.
